answers.question: Within how many minutes must a mine operator call MSHA after an accident that kills a miner?
answers.answer: The operator must contact MSHA immediately, and within 15 minutes, once the operator knows or should know that an accident involving a death has occurred.

claims.text: The operator must contact MSHA immediately and within 15 minutes once the operator knows or should know of an accident involving a death at the mine.
claims.quote: The operator shall immediately contact MSHA at once without delay and within 15 minutes at the toll-free number, 1-800-746-1553, once the operator knows or should know that an accident has occurred involving:

claims.text: The accidents covered include a death of an individual at the mine.
claims.quote: (a) A death of an individual at the mine;

answers.question: What minimum incombustible content must the combined dust in an underground coal mine keep where no methane is present?
answers.answer: Where no methane is present, the incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust must be not less than 80 percent.

claims.text: The incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust must be not less than 80 percent; it is increased only where methane is present.
claims.quote: the incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust shall be not less than 80 percent. Where methane is present in any ventilating current, the percent of incombustible content of such combined dust shall be increased 0.4 percent for each 0.1 percent of methane.

answers.question: How long must the self-rescue device given to each underground coal miner be able to protect that person?
answers.answer: The self-rescue device must be adequate to protect the person for 1 hour or longer. Under 30 CFR 75.1714, the operator must make available to each miner who goes underground an approved self-rescue device adequate to protect that person for 1 hour or longer.

claims.text: Each operator must make available to each underground miner an approved self-rescue device adequate to protect the person for 1 hour or longer.
claims.quote: Each operator shall make available to each miner who goes underground, and to visitors authorized to enter the mine by the operator, an approved self-rescue device or devices which is adequate to protect such person for 1 hour or longer.

answers.question: How often must an underground metal or nonmetal mine hold evacuation drills?
answers.answer: Underground metal or nonmetal mines must hold mine evacuation drills at least once every six months. Each drill must be held for each shift at some time other than a shift change.

claims.text: Mine evacuation drills must be held at least once every six months.
claims.quote: At least once every six months, mine evacuation drills shall be held

claims.text: Drills must be held for each shift at some time other than a shift change.
claims.quote: Be held for each shift at some time other than a shift change and involve all persons underground;

answers.question: How many hours of training must a new underground miner receive before being assigned to work duties?
answers.answer: A new underground miner must receive no less than 40 hours of training before being assigned to work duties (30 CFR 48.5).

claims.text: Each new miner must receive no less than 40 hours of training before being assigned to work duties.
claims.quote: Each new miner shall receive no less than 40 hours of training as prescribed in this section before such miner is assigned to work duties.

answers.question: What is the permissible exposure level for noise at a mine, as an 8-hour average?
answers.answer: The chunks do not state the numeric permissible exposure level as an 8-hour average.

answers.question: How high must berms or guardrails be on the banks of roadways at metal and nonmetal mines?
answers.answer: Berms or guardrails at metal and nonmetal mines must be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway (30 CFR 57.9300(b)). The surface-mine standard, 56.9300, has the same requirement.

claims.text: Berms or guardrails must be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.
claims.quote: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.

answers.question: For how many hours must the breathable air in an approved refuge alternative sustain each person?
answers.answer: The breathable air must sustain each person for 96 hours.

claims.text: Within the refuge alternative, the breathable air must sustain each person for 96 hours.
claims.quote: The breathable air sustains each person for 96 hours,

answers.question: At what depth does OSHA require a construction trench to have a protective system such as shoring or a trench box?
answers.answer: The provided chunks do not say at what depth OSHA requires a construction trench to have a protective system such as shoring or a trench box. They cover MSHA mining rules on slopes and shafts, shaft-sinking buckets, and roll-over protective structures. None of them addresses trenching.

answers.question: When does a mine need an EPA stormwater discharge permit for runoff from its site?
answers.answer: The provided chunks don't say when a mine needs an EPA stormwater discharge permit. They cover other permits: MSHA permits for experimental electric face equipment, permits for mining near bodies of water, and impoundment design requirements.
